events.description: 16. MINUTE entry before the Honorable Franklin U. Valderrama: Before the Court are Plaintiffs' emergency motion for a preliminary injunction 4 and memorandum in support 5 . Although the motion consists primarily of background, it also contains some substantive argument, as does, predictably, the memorandum in support. Although the motion and memorandum each consist of less than 15 pages, together they total 27 pages, which exceeds the 15-page limit set by N.D. Ill. Local Rule 7.1. In order to streamline briefing on Plaintiffs' motion, on or before 8/13/2026, the Court directs Plaintiffs to file one motion or memorandum in support that includes all of the relevant background and argument necessary to decide their motion. Such a renewed motion may be accompanied by a motion for leave to file excess pages, if necessary. The Court terminate Plaintiffs' motion for an emergency preliminary injunction 4 for failure to comply with Local Rule 7.1. The Court sets the following expedited briefing schedule on Plaintiffs' forthcoming renewed motion for an emergency preliminary injunction: Defendants' response due on or before 8/21/2026; Plaintiffs' reply due on or before 8/26/2026. Additionally, it does not appear that summons have issued (and correspondingly, that Defendants have been served). Although the motion and memorandum contain certificates of service showing service by electronic means to counsel for the Illinois State Board of Elections and its members and counsel for the election authorities for the 4th Congressional District, given the emergent nature of Plaintiffs' request, Plaintiffs should endeavor to formally serve Defendants as soon as possible. The Court directs Plaintiffs to serve this Minute Entry on Defendants on or before 8/13/2026 and to file a certificate of service on the docket. Such service of the Minute Entry may be effectuated by electronic means. Mailed notice. (jcm) (Entered: 08/12/2026)

events.description: 24. MINUTE entry before the Honorable Franklin U. Valderrama: For the reasons stated in the motion, and in particular based on Plaintiffs' own delay in filing their motion for a preliminary injunction (that is, the motion was not filed until over three weeks after Defendants declined to certify Plaintiff Sigcho Lopez for the November 2026 ballot, and nearly two weeks after Plaintiffs filed their complaint), the Court grants Defendants' opposed motion for extension of time to file their combined response to Plaintiffs' motion for a preliminary injunction and motion to dismiss 23 . The Court modifies the briefing schedule on Plaintiffs' preliminary injunction motion as follows: Defendants' response is due on or before 8/28/2026; Plaintiffs' reply is due on or before 9/2/2026. The Court sets the following briefing schedule on Defendants' anticipated motion to dismiss: Plaintiffs' response is due on or before 9/11/2026; Defendants' reply is due on or before 9/18/2026. Mailed notice. (jcm) (Entered: 08/21/2026)

events.description: 43. MINUTE entry before the Honorable Franklin U. Valderrama: For the reasons stated in the motion, the Court grants Plaintiffs' unopposed motion for extension of time to file their amended complaint 42 . The Court considers Plaintiffs' amended complaint 41 to be timely filed. Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(3), Defendants' answer or other responsive pleading is due on or before 11/4/2026. The Court also notes that a joint initial status report was due on 10/19/2026 2 . To date, no joint initial status report has been filed. Given the filing of the amended complaint and the responsive pleading deadline, the Court sua sponte extends the deadline for the filing of the joint initial status report to 11/13/2026. The Court expects the parties to comply with all Court-ordered deadlines going forward. Mailed notice. (jcm) (Entered: 10/22/2026)
